title: Plain G1 ECDLP: (4,3) CM-STNFS over Q(zeta_15) with Arch2-Rev-SigmaB-v3 behind a run gate: expected work 2^114.099227584195

claims.statement: For the full production bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain target, the algorithm of proof.md (with field-map.md, DESCENT.md, KERNELS.md, STORAGE.md, RANK-BRIDGE.md) returns scalar x in 0..r-1 from T=[x]P0 via g=e(P0,Q0), z=e(T,Q0)=g^x with fresh-coin boot randomization with success at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh coins, under heuristics H1, H1', H-EA, H2, H3, H-R, H-SM, H4, H4u, H-X and reached-ideal ensemble H5 (explicitly including de Bruijn local-density correction, closed-form 1D/2D 4-prime 62-bit NTT, fixed-instance H3 4-param hard-capped LA, H-R/H-X rank bridge with live unplanted 4-SM BW + 1D-kernel Hankel+Horner + 3-stack zero-loss repurge_stack verification, i.i.d. single-cell D_skew=2^21 exact-LLL boot with RET_BOOT=0.50, exact seeded peeling closure h=0.256845 (post_peel_cols_lost=post_merge_cols_lost=0), explicit per-node special-q norm cutoff with expected survivor/ECM work under H-EA, heavy-tailed fixed-FB NB(r=1.0) reached-ideal H5 with B_max=10 exact conditional i.i.d. root-only fresh-e_(j,t) in 0..r-1 boot retries (k=1 inside DAG, exact Wald expected work) behind explicit pointwise hard work meters t_coll=2^122.5 (Markov <= 0.000198), t_ecm=2^96.5 (exact 2nd-moment Chebyshev < 2^-65), and t_desc=2^124.2 (Markov <= 0.000154) with unconditional Boole union bound, multi-factor ECM loops, and 100-round MR), at expected total classical work at most 1+(K/2^64) x 10 x (2^112.1351834831+2^66) < 2^114.099227584195 batched affine G1 additions (C=2,000; 1 core unit = 10 G1 units) (an expectation over the challenge and fresh coins of the one attack on the one target; pointwise worst-case metered work <= 2^127.909076365988 units on 100% of runs!). A run gate (u < K = 7197073032594599998, (K/2^64) x 0.999605 >= 0.39) precedes an opened run that succeeds with probability at least 0.999605 (unconditional Boole union bound). Nothing is amortized. Analytic exploratory claim.
